thread:
incident-bot: ALERT fired -> service: api-edge-eu, symptom: intermittent 503 / TLS handshake failures from ALB health checks. PagerDuty: PD-INC-98234 https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-98234 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Automated page: team=network-sre, severity=sev2, policy=lb-health-failover. Notified: eric (oncall) -> escalation in 5m if unacked.

eric (oncall): acked the page. I'm looking. Any rollback/traffic-shift play already in motion?

maria (support): getting a handful of customer reports — EU region: ~5% 503s on inference endpoints, a few enterprise customers seeing timeouts. Logged support ticket IDs: SUP-4231, SUP-4232.

network-sre: seeing repeated TLS handshake errors from ALB to backend pool. Health check connections get TLS alert 40 (handshake failure). Not seeing backend app crashes. Likely cert mismatch or backend TLS config change.

samir: recent deploy? any cert rotations last hour? I pushed a small nginx config change in eu-canary 3h ago but that was green. Checking cert manager logs now.

jen (ops-lead): tagging this as potential config/regression until proven otherwise. If LB can't validate health, we should consider moving traffic to eu-secondary pool. Can someone validate healthy targets?

network-sre: grabbed curl from ALB to backend IP (port 443) -> shows TLS handshake failure: ```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.12.34.56:443 -servername api-eu.redwood.example
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735212345152:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:../ssl/record/ssl3_record.c:252
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

eric (oncall): running probe against other targets in pool... some targets return normal cert chain, others fail. Might be a subset with expired/incorrect cert. Querying cert info: `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect ip:443 -servername ...`

samir: cert-manager logs show a failing renewal job for instance-group eu-pool-3 at 2026-03-15T02:41Z — looks like ACME rate limit error. Renewal didn't complete, so that pool kept an old cert that expired at 2026-03-15T03:00Z. That matches timeline.

jen (ops-lead): ok, plan: 1) remove eu-pool-3 from LB rotation (weight 0) 2) confirm traffic shift to eu-pool-1/2 3) trigger emergency cert reissue for eu-pool-3 and re-register when fixed. Who can execute 1-2?

eric (oncall): I'll do the weight shift now. Command: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=weight,Value=0` (we use our internal wrapper: `rctl lb weight-set eu-pool-3 0`). Doing it.

incident-bot: ACTION -> weight-set job queued: rctl job 87219. Watch: https://runbook.redwood/job/87219

network-sre: after weight shift, observed error rate drop in metrics for EU API requests within 30s. Topline impact dropped from ~5% to ~0.4% 503s. Good. Continue to monitor.

maria (support): sending customer updates: "We detected and mitigated an EU edge TLS issue impacting a subset of requests. Traffic has been shifted and we continue to remediate the affected pool. ETA for full resolution ~40m."

samir: cert reissue started using emergency ACME path: `kubectl -n certs exec -it certbot-emer -- acme renew --force --domain api-eu.redwood.example --group eu-pool-3` — started at 03:12Z. If renewal fails, fallback is to import last-known-good cert from vault and rotate quickly.

jen (ops-lead): escalate to infra for rate limit investigation, we can't keep hitting ACME limits. @infra-team please advise on emergency import path.

infra (via network-sre): recommend import from Vault backup. Preparing cert bundle. ETA 10m. File: /vault/certs/eu-pool-3/backup-20260228.pem

samir: imported backup cert into instance-group eu-pool-3, reloaded nginx, health checks now passing on those targets. Example command: `rctl ssh eu-pool-3 'sudo systemctl reload nginx && curl -vI https://127.0.0.1:8443'` — 200 OK locally.

eric (oncall): re-adding eu-pool-3 to LB at 10% weight then ramping: `rctl lb weight-set eu-pool-3 10` -> monitor.

incident-bot: PD update: PD-INC-98234 -> acknowledged by eric (oncall). Status: mitigated -> partial. Escalation timer paused.

network-sre: after adding back, health checks stable and TLS chain looks correct. Observed a small bump in 4xx for a few minutes during ramp but no 5xx spike.

maria (support): updating customers: full service restored for most users; we will follow up with post-incident note describing root cause (failed cert renewal + ACME rate limits) and remediation plan.

samir: filing follow-up RFC: ensure emergency import path documented, adjust cert-manager retry/alerting, and schedule staggered renewals for pool groups to avoid batch ACME limits. Also adding probe to detect any non-uniform cert expiry across pool within 24h window.

jen (ops-lead): severity downgraded to sev3. Please add timeline and notify CS+sales for any high-touch customers. Marking for postmortem if impact > 1% for >15m (we were above that briefly).

eric (oncall): handing off to samir for remediation and postmortem. I'm un-acking and going offline for on-call rotation. :wave:

samir: thanks — I'll own the postmortem and remediation. Pulling logs and will create INC-98234-ticket with timeline and remediation tasks.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for active paging. PD-INC-98234 -> status: monitoring. If errors cross threshold again, auto-page will resume.

jen (ops-lead): nice work team. Add runbook updates and note ACME limits in the postmortem.

maria (support): closing related support tickets and emailing affected customers with timeline + mitigation steps done.

eric (oncall): final note — if anyone needs me to re-open PD or coordinate handoff next shift ping me. Good job. :thumbsup:
